evals.prompt: We need a 2-minute product demo video for our SaaS homepage. What's the fastest way to produce it?
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first and name a lane from tools/video/ROUTING.md before picking an engine. Should walk through the Product Demo Video workflow: script the key features and value props (cross-reference copywriting skill), screen record the product flow, programmatic overlay on the code lane that fits (brag only if it is a 15–25s share clip of this project; Hyperframes for a one-off HTML composition; Remotion if the demo is a template you will keep), optional AI B-roll with Veo/Runway for establishing shots, voiceover via recording or AI avatar (HeyGen) for narration, export at platform-appropriate specs (16:9 for homepage). Should not recommend Hyperframes as the default agent engine. Should remind: don't use AI for product UI screens (models hallucinate UI) — use real screen recording. Should mention captions are essential (85% of social video watched without sound — applies to homepage too).
assertions: Walks through Product Demo workflow steps
Uses real screen recording, not AI generated UI

evals.prompt: We want to make weekly product update videos. About 60 seconds each. Don't want to be on camera. Recommend a setup.
evals.expected_output: Should name the avatar lane from tools/video/ROUTING.md given recurring weekly cadence and no-camera preference. Should recommend HeyGen specifically: best lip-sync, has an MCP server (so agents can generate videos directly), 230+ avatars, 140+ languages, Creator plan supports unlimited 5-minute videos. Should explain custom avatars (upload 2-5 min of yourself for a digital twin) as an option for brand consistency. Should outline the recurring pipeline: script written from product context, HeyGen generates avatar video, optional programmatic overlay on the code lane that fits (Remotion when the same layout repeats each week), export and distribute. Should mention this is exactly the case where AI avatars shine vs other approaches (recurring content, multilingual versions, personalized outreach at scale). Should warn: if authentic founder content matters more than scale, film yourself instead.
assertions: Mentions HeyGen MCP server for agents
Identifies as a recurring use case

evals.prompt: I want to generate a 10-second clip of a person typing on a laptop in a coffee shop for our landing page. Which AI tool?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the AI Video Generation model comparison. Should recommend Veo 3 for highest quality with synced audio, Runway Gen-4 for motion control and temporal consistency (~10 sec/gen sweet spot), or Kling 3.0 for lower-cost volume production. Should give a structured video prompt example following Subject + Action + Camera + Style + Mood pattern: 'A close-up shot of hands typing on a laptop keyboard in a cozy coffee shop, shallow depth of field, warm afternoon lighting through a window, camera holds steady, cinematic color grading, 4K.' Should warn about common mistakes: too vague, ignoring camera movement, forgetting style, requesting readable text. Should mention Sora has had limited availability — check current status.
assertions: Follows Subject + Action + Camera + Style + Mood pattern

evals.prompt: We just did a 60-minute webinar. How do we get short clips out of it for social?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Repurposing Workflow: long-form content → Descript (clean up, remove filler, polish) → Opus Clip (auto-extract 5-10 best moments, scores virality potential) → CapCut (add captions, effects, platform styling) → distribute to TikTok, Reels, Shorts, LinkedIn. Should explain when to use each tool: Descript for transcript-based editing, Opus Clip for finding the best moments at scale, CapCut for platform-native polish, Captions.ai for auto-captions and eye-contact correction if needed. Should mention 85% of social video is watched without sound — captions are essential. Should mention aspect ratio matters: 9:16 for TikTok/Reels/Shorts, 1:1 or 9:16 for LinkedIn. Should recommend hooking in the first 3 seconds — cross-reference social skill.
assertions: Names Descript, Opus Clip, CapCut in sequence

evals.prompt: We need to generate 50 personalized intro videos for sales outreach. Each one mentions a different company name and pain point.
evals.expected_output: Should read tools/video/ROUTING.md and split lanes: avatar narration is HeyGen; a repeated overlay with per-company data is the Remotion lane. Should explain: prepare a master script template with variables, run a loop generating 50 HeyGen videos each with a personalized script, optional Remotion overlays for company logo or visual context. Should note HeyGen is well-suited to personalized outreach at scale and has an MCP server. Should warn about quality tradeoffs at volume and recommend testing the first 5 manually before generating all 50. Should mention reply tracking to measure ROI vs cold text emails — these are expensive to produce so should outperform email significantly to justify the effort. Should mention captions for the videos.
assertions: Splits avatar (HeyGen) and repeated overlay (Remotion) using tools/video/ROUTING.md

evals.prompt: Should I use Hyperframes or Remotion for programmatic video?
evals.expected_output: Should refuse a default and apply tools/video/ROUTING.md. Should name /brag when the job is a 15–25s share clip of the current project. Should name Hyperframes when the job is a one-off HTML composition (explainer, PR, slideshow, captions, short motion, or a launch longer than 25s). Should name Remotion when the video is an asset you keep: props, batch, 3D, Studio, or Lambda. Should mention Remotion's company license above 3 people. Should ask which of those situations this video is.
assertions: Names /brag for a 15–25s launch clip of this project
Names Hyperframes for a one-off HTML composition
Names Remotion for a kept template, batch, or Lambda
Does not recommend Hyperframes as the default agent engine
Asks which situation this video is
